impact.rationale: The production parser is shared by sealed-archive decoders and changes the externally observed archive error code for token-budget exhaustion. A regression would be bounded to archive admission/decoding but could misclassify inputs or reject valid boundary data.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The change is narrow and source-complete across all four token-consumption error sites, but the directly relevant Go test was not run for these exact afterimages.

regressionProtection.rationale: The existing exact-boundary and array-close assertions are retained and three focused one-over assertions cover value, object-close, and object-key sites. Static inventory proves the same 491 required tops, but no exact-candidate Go/gofmt execution is available.

recoverability.rationale: The patch changes two source files, adds no migration or persisted representation, and can be reverted without data replay.

confidence.rationale: Receipt hashes, Git blobs, LF bytes, exact base, diff scope, callers, error paths, and symbolic token counts are independently verified; runtime execution remains intentionally unavailable.

applicability.rationale: sealedArchiveScanJSON is the production scanner used by sealedArchiveDecode and the failed P207 top is the directly changed boundary test.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: At exact c648, P207 reports the primitive/name boundary top failed; base code collapses token-budget errors arising at value/key/close consumption into subscription_archive_invalid instead of preserving subscription_archive_limit.

riskDrivers: Error-code behavior is a caller-visible contract.
The scanner is shared by persisted and non-persisted archive decoding.
Exact candidate Go and gofmt checks were not run.
protectiveFactors: Raw json.Decoder errors are normalized to subscription_archive_invalid inside nextToken before propagation.
The token ceiling remains 1,048,576 and is checked before each decoder.Token call.
Existing exact-boundary and array-close one-over assertions remain, with three additional consumption-site assertions.
No top-level test name, skip, limit constant, persistence format, or caller signature changes.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Malformed JSON remains subscription_archive_invalid while every internal token-budget overflow remains subscription_archive_limit.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: A decoder syntax error at an object key or closing delimiter could be returned directly and escape as an unclassified/raw error or be mistaken for a budget error.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: nextToken converts every decoder.Token error to sealedArchiveFail(CodeArchiveInvalid); visit only propagates this normalized invalid error or its own pre-decode CodeArchiveLimit.

materialBoundaries.invariant: Exactly 1,048,576 JSON tokens are accepted and the 1,048,577th token is rejected at every consumption site.
materialBoundaries.counterexample: An off-by-one at a primitive value, object key, object close, or array close could accept one extra token or reject the exact boundary.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: tokens increments before every decoder.Token call and rejects when greater than sealedArchiveTokenMax; symbolic construction proves boundary=1,048,576 and each one-over fixture fails at count 1,048,577.

unknowns.summary: Exact candidate compilation, gofmt cleanliness, and execution of the focused Go top are not observed in this source-only review; they remain required integration gates rather than a source-visible defect.
